results.reasoning: Equation (1) defines T_η^{0,1}M as the intersection of the complexified tangent space ℂ⊗T_ηM with the span of antiholomorphic vector fields ∂/∂z̄_j. This is the standard definition in CR geometry of the (0,1) tangent space. While slightly nonstandard in notation (usually ℂ⊗_ℝ T_ηM is written), the definition is mathematically correct. No error detected.

Equation (2) defines the disc hull DH(X) as the set of points through which there exists an analytic disc attached to X. This is a standard set-theoretic definition, consistent with the preceding paragraph's definition of analytic discs. No mathematical error.

Equation (3) defines DH^k(X) as the k-fold iteration of the disc hull operator DH. This is a recursive definition: DH^1(X)=DH(X), DH^{k+1}(X)=DH(DH^k(X)). The notation with the underbrace 'k times' is clear and mathematically sound. No error.

Equation (4) defines SADH_q(X), the shrinking approximate disc hull. The definition requires a continuous family φ_t of analytic discs parameterized by t∈[0,1] with: φ_t(∂𝔻)⊂X_ε, φ₀≡q, z=φ₁(0), and ‖φ_t(0)−q‖ strictly increasing. This is a valid set-theoretic definition. The conditions are well-formed: φ_t are maps from the unit disc 𝔻 to ℂⁿ, holomorphic on the interior and continuous on the closure, with boundaries within ε of X. The requirement that the family shrinks from q (φ₀≡q) and ‖φ_t(0)−q‖ increases strictly ensures the 'shrinking' property. No mathematical error.

Equation (5) defines the set X = {z ∈ ℂ³ : z₁ ∈ ∂𝔻, z₂ = φ_k(z₁), z₃ = 1/k, k ∈ ℕ} for Example 3.9. This constructs a countable union of curves in ℂ³. Each k gives a curve (graph of φ_k over ∂𝔻) at height z₃ = 1/k. The set definition is mathematically well-formed. The convergence properties of φ_k are described in the surrounding text, not in the equation itself. No error.

Equation (7): φₙ(ζ) = (1/√n ζ, 1/n, 1/n). This gives an analytic disc where |z|² = |1/√n ζ|² = 1/n on ∂𝔻 (since |ζ|=1 on ∂𝔻), so w₁ = |z|² = 1/n. The condition w₂ = |z|² + f(|z|²)(Re z) = 1/n + f(1/n)(Re z) = 1/n since f(1/n) = 0 by construction. This is mathematically consistent with the construction in Example 3.11. Note: the equation numbering skips from (5) to (7) — equation (6) appears to belong to a section not included in this paper excerpt (likely Section 4). This is a numbering gap, not a mathematical error in this equation.

Equation (8) defines X = X₁ ∪ X₂ as the union of two toroidal sets in ℂ². X₁ is the portion of the unit torus (|z₁|=|z₂|=1) with Im z₂ ≥ 0, and X₂ is the cylinder-torus product (|z₁|=2, |z₂|=1) with Im z₂ < 0. The two sets are disjoint in the z₁-coordinate (1 vs 2) but share the same z₂-domain. The definition is well-formed. No mathematical error.

Equation (9) computes DH(X) from equation (8). The reasoning in the text is sound: for discs attached to X₁, φ₂ must be constant (since Im φ₂ ≥ 0 on ∂𝔻 and |φ₂|=1, a nonconstant Blaschke product would cover the full circle, contradicting the sign restriction). The disc fills in |z₁|≤1. Similarly for X₂, φ₂ is constant, filling |z₁|≤2. Minor precision note: the second set's Im z₂ condition is written as ≤0, whereas from X₂ strictly, one only gets Im z₂ < 0 (the boundary Im z₂ = 0 is in the closure, not necessarily in DH(X) itself). This is a minor imprecision, not a mathematical error requiring correction, especially under lenient strictness.

Equation (10) defines X' ⊂ ℂ³ as a scaled version of Example 3.13's X, with z₃ acting as a real scaling parameter in [0,1]. At z₃=1, this reduces to equation (8) scaled by z₃. At z₃=0, both components collapse to the origin. The definition uses |z₁|=|z₂|=Re z₃ and |z₁|=2Re z₃, |z₂|=Re z₃ with z₃∈[0,1] (real interval). Since z₃ is real, Re z₃ = z₃, so the scaling is linear. The definition is mathematically consistent. No error.

Equation (11) defines X ⊂ ℂ³ for Example 3.14. This is the union of two families of curves parameterized by t∈[0,1] and ζ∈∂𝔻. At t=0: z₁=z₂=0, z₃=1 (both families). At t=1: z₃=-1 (both families, since e^{iπ}=e^{-iπ}=-1). The two paths from z₃=1 to z₃=-1 go through the upper and lower half-planes respectively (e^{iπt} vs e^{-iπt}), creating different analytic continuation paths. This construction is mathematically sound and serves its purpose of demonstrating non-unique extension. No error.

Equation (12) is the filled-in version of equation (11), replacing ∂𝔻 with 𝔻 (the open unit disc). This represents the disc hull: for each t, the disc ζ→(tζ,0,e^{iπt}) fills the ball of radius t in the z₁-plane, and similarly for the second family. The set definition is well-formed. The point (0,0,-1) is reached when t=1, ζ=0. The construction correctly demonstrates that SADH_q(X) contains this set but functions from CR_H(X) may not extend uniquely. No error.

summary.minor_issue_detail: Equation (9): minor imprecision using ≤ instead of < for Im z₂ in second union component (boundary is in closure, not necessarily in DH(X) — not errata-worthy under lenient strictness)
